errors.evidence: The light blue bar, representing the baseline model, is visually the longest bar in every group, extending to the most negative value on the y-axis. The description incorrectly states it is the shortest.

errors.evidence: In the chart, the bars for models fine-tuned on their corresponding specialty are the shortest (ending at the highest, least negative y-value), not the tallest. For example, in the 'Pediatrics' group, the dark brown bar is the shortest. The description incorrectly inverts the visual representation.

errors.text_span: In general, the fine-tuned models exhibit improved performance (lower negative log-probabilities) in their corresponding specialty, with the most significant improvements observed when the model is fine-tuned on the same specialty as the test tokens.
errors.evidence: This sentence offers a conclusion about the data, using evaluative language like 'improved performance' and 'most significant improvements'. A neutral description should state the visual facts (e.g., 'the bar for the model fine-tuned on a specialty is the shortest in its corresponding group') without interpreting them as 'improvement'.
